title: Vandal Hearts II
subtitle: A tactical journey through a divided country
summary: Vandal Hearts II is Konami's PlayStation tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 8 July 1999. The player follows a group of characters through a political conflict, travelling between towns and battlefields as the story develops. Its grid-based encounters make position and anticipation central to progress. Moving one member of the party is a decision about what the enemy may do as well as where the ally should stand. The sequel gives the familiar tactical structure a particular uncertainty, asking the player to plan around an opponent who is also preparing to move.
body: Vandal Hearts II is Konami's PlayStation tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 8 July 1999. The player follows a group of characters through a political conflict, travelling between towns and battlefields as the story develops. Its grid-based encounters make position and anticipation central to progress. Moving one member of the party is a decision about what the enemy may do as well as where the ally should stand. The sequel gives the familiar tactical structure a particular uncertainty, asking the player to plan around an opponent who is also preparing to move.

The battle system links the player's selected action to an enemy action, making prediction part of every exchange. A target may change position, and a seemingly safe destination can become dangerous once both sides have acted. Equipment determines important aspects of a character's capabilities, allowing the party to be adjusted for the next encounter. The player therefore prepares in two ways: choosing the tools carried into battle and learning how to read an enemy's likely response. A useful plan has to account for movement that has not yet happened.

An overworld map connects towns and combat areas, with many locations available for return visits. Towns provide the intervals in which the party can gather information and prepare, while newly opened destinations carry the story forward. Takashi Takeda designed the game and Hiroshi Tamawari composed its music. North America received it in December 1999, followed by PAL territories in June 2000. Within the tactical role-playing genre, its distinctive contribution is the pressure placed on prediction: the grid is not only a set of current positions but a place whose next arrangement must be imagined.
story_headings: A tactical journey through a divided country
A move has to survive the enemy response
Travel gives the battles their place
